result.title: Does coverage explain core-set active learning? Mean, max, and the choice of distance
result.summary: Core-set selection casts batch active learning as a covering problem, in which the points to label minimise the covering radius of the pool. Its main argument is a generalization bound in which this radius controls the gap between the loss on the pool and on the labelled sample. We examine what this bound requires and what it says in practice. We first state it with the assumption that its proof uses at the labelled points, a zero conditional risk, and show that it then holds for any dissimilarity and any selection rule that uses no label outside the sample. The proof works point by point and involves two averages, the mean distance of the pool to the labelled sample and the purity of the cells attached to the labelled points. Keeping them gives, when labels are deterministic at the labelled points, a bound on the pool loss with no zero-loss assumption and without the factor C, the number of classes, of the original constant. We then compare scales, for deterministic labels and a regression function Lipschitz on the whole pool. With the original constant, the bound can be informative only if the radius is below the smallest distance between two classes divided by C. Without C, its radius form can be informative only once the nearest-neighbour rule built on the sample is exact on the pool. Finally, a misalignment criterion measures whether a quantity ranks selections as the gap or the test error do. Experiments on a Gaussian pool and on two image pools, digits and MNIST, the latter under eight distances, and with a network retrained at each cycle, show that the radius does not rank selections consistently with the gap and, on the image pools, that the bounds that do not use the labels of the pool are never informative and that covering in mean rather than in maximum, as greedy k-medoids does, gives a higher purity and accuracy than random sampling.

AI.brief_summary: 该文重新审视 core-set 主动学习的覆盖论证：给出不依赖零风险假设的更紧泛化界，比较「均值覆盖」与「最大覆盖」的可信息尺度，并提出错位准则检验覆盖半径能否像池上损失间隙或测试误差那样给选择排序；在高斯池与 digits、MNIST 图像池上实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“覆盖是均值还是最大值”“代理排序是否与真实误差一致”的检验思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据/支持集筛选准则的有效性；但原文针对池式训练样本选择，迁移到推理期证据获取需再判断。
